- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of sustainable fashion materials that have become more widely adopted in the past decade include organic cotton, hemp, recycled polyester, and Tencel.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Organic cotton is grown without harmful pesticides and chemicals, reducing the carbon footprint and pollution.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Hemp requires less water, energy, and pesticides than many other crops and can be used for various products.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recycled polyester is made from recycled plastic bottles and reduces plastic waste in landfills and waterways.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tencel is biodegradable, requires less energy and water to produce, and does not use harmful chemicals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The adoption of sustainable materials positively impacts the environment and promotes ethical practices in the fashion industry.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Sustainable materials have improved in quality, variety, texture, and aesthetics, offering style and comfort comparable to traditional materials.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tencel has a silky texture and can be used for elegant designs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Many fashion brands are incorporating sustainable materials into their designs, making stylish options available.
- [USER] The user has heard that sustainable materials can be more expensive and is looking for ways to incorporate sustainable fashion into their wardrobe without overspending.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Sustainable materials can be more expensive due to costly production methods and smaller quantities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggestions for incorporating sustainable fashion affordably include shopping secondhand or thrift, investing in quality pieces, shopping for off-season items, and researching ethical brands.
